source_claim: Select the next paper-reproduction probe by expected reduction in adoption decision loss per unit cost and stop with adopt, reject, or inconclusive.

axes.problem: Spend a limited budget on cheap observations before deciding whether to run or adopt an expensive method.
axes.mechanism: Bayesian posterior decision risk, value-of-information-per-cost acquisition, and three-way sequential stopping.
axes.insight: The cheapest faithful check need not be the most decision-informative check.
axes.application: Paper-derived intervention probes on user tasks.
axes.evaluation_scope: Cost to correct adoption decision under fixed false-adoption and false-rejection constraints.

comparisons.title: Cost-Sensitive Multi-Fidelity Bayesian Optimization with Transfer of Learning Curve Extrapolation
comparisons.evidence: The abstract already defines a user cost-performance utility, selects future observations with a cost-sensitive acquisition function, transfers cheap-to-expensive predictions, and stops automatically; the candidate changes the application object but not the central sequential decision mechanism.
comparisons.limitations: Full text was not fetched, but the abstract states all load-bearing mechanism components.

comparisons.title: GPTuneBand: Multi-task and Multi-fidelity Autotuning for Large-scale High Performance Computing Applications
comparisons.evidence: It combines multi-task Bayesian optimization and multi-armed-bandit fidelity allocation under limited budget.
comparisons.limitations: It optimizes configurations rather than paper adoption.

comparisons.title: Efficient Bayesian Learning Curve Extrapolation using Prior-Data Fitted Networks
comparisons.evidence: It builds a Bayesian posterior predictive from cheap prefixes and uses it for model selection and early stopping.
comparisons.limitations: The observation family is a learning curve rather than heterogeneous paper probes.

limitations: Candidate-specific external collision terms were not transmitted; the assessment reuses generic run-scoped searches.
The central mechanism appears to be a direct application of established cost-sensitive Bayesian optimal experimental design and active hypothesis testing.
